newsitem.title: UK: Publisher Reed Elseview profits gain.
newsitem.headline: Publisher Reed Elseview profits gain.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed Elsevier Plc reported an 11 percent rise in 1996 profits Wednesday but warned that currency exchange rates could depress this year's earnings.

Reed Elsevier Co-Chairman Nigel Stapleton told Reuters the strength of the British pound would, if maintained, "drag down" its earnings by 5 percent this year. Earnings figures for the combined businesses of Reed Elsevier are expressed in sterling.

Pre-tax profits rose to 805 million pounds ($1.3 billion) from 723 million ($1.15 billion). Revenue from continuing operations rose to 3.38 billion pounds ($5.37 billion) from 3.21 billion ($5.10 billion). Analysts had forecast profits of between 808 million ($1.28 billion) and 821 million pounds ($1.31 billion).
Analysts said the company's performance had fallen slightly short of expectations and that Reed shares had risen more than 10 percent over the last two months on takeover speculation.
The company noted that currency conversions meant that Elsevier results and dividends were helped in guilder terms.
"It's good news for Elsevier and bad for Reed," said co-chairman Stapleton.

Stapleton said the 1996 figures reflected a "solid performance" right across the group. They followed a 4 percent earnings dilution resulting from the company's 1995 consumer business divestment programme.
Reed Elsevier sold consumer businesses, such as local newspapers, in order to focus on the provision of information in fields like science, business and the legal profession.
Reed Elsevier said it remained committed to an active acquisition policy. He noted the company had spent over 300 million pounds ($477 million) on some 20 transactions in 1996.
Stapleton said a "big deal" such as Reed's $1.5 billion purchase of U.S. on-line information supplier LEXIS-NEXIS in 1994 would be "nice but not necessary."
